wiki_overview.content:
<blog>

# Findora: AI-Powered Missing Persons Reunification Platform

## Project Introduction

Findora is a Next.js-based web application designed to reunite missing persons with their families using automated AI facial recognition technology. The platform provides a privacy-first approach to connecting reported missing persons with public sightings, leveraging client-side face embedding generation and server-side matching algorithms.

### Core Goals and Objectives
- **Privacy-First Design**: All photos remain private and are never publicly listed
- **AI-Powered Matching**: Automated facial recognition to identify potential matches between missing person reports and public sightings  
- **Secure Communication**: Controlled contact sharing only when strong matches are detected
- **Real-time Updates**: Live dashboard showing match progress and case status

### Target Audience
- **Families/Reporters**: Individuals reporting missing loved ones who need immediate assistance in locating them
- **Public/Finders**: Community members who may have spotted missing persons and want to help
- **Law Enforcement**: Organizations coordinating search and rescue operations

## Technical Architecture

The application follows a modern Next.js App Router architecture with a clear separation between client-side and server-side responsibilities:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Client Browser] --> B[Next.js Pages]
    B --> C[API Routes]
    C --> D[Supabase Database]
    B --> E[Face API Client-Side]
    E --> F[Local Face Embeddings]
    C --> G[Server-Side Processing]
    G --> D
    D --> H[Storage Buckets]
```

### Component Breakdown

**Frontend Layer (Next.js App Router)**
- Client components for interactive UI elements
- Server components for data fetching and initial page rendering
- Dynamic imports for browser-only libraries like Leaflet maps

**Backend Layer (API Routes)**
- RESTful API endpoints for authentication, data management, and business logic
- Server-side face matching algorithms
- Database query optimization and security enforcement

**Data Layer (Supabase)**
- PostgreSQL database with Row Level Security (RLS) policies
- File storage for case and sighting photos
- Real-time capabilities for live updates

### Design Patterns

1. **Component-Based Architecture**: Reusable React components with clear separation of concerns
2. **Server-Client Split**: Heavy processing on server, lightweight operations on client
3. **Security-First Approach**: RLS policies and token-based authentication
4. **Progressive Enhancement**: Graceful degradation when face detection fails

## Key Implementation

### Main Entry Points
- **Application Root**: `app/layout.tsx` - Global layout configuration with metadata and analytics
- **Home Page**: `app/page.tsx` - Landing page with real-time statistics and call-to-action buttons
- **Dashboard**: `app/dashboard/page.tsx` - Dual-role interface for both reporters and finders

### Core Modules

**Authentication & Authorization**
- Supabase Auth integration with custom middleware
- Role-based access control for different user types
- Secure session management with JWT tokens

**Face Recognition System**
- Client-side face embedding generation using @vladmandic/face-api
- Local model loading for offline capability
- 128-dimensional vector embeddings for similarity matching

**Database Schema**
- Comprehensive table structure with proper relationships
- Row Level Security policies for data isolation
- Automatic profile creation triggers

### Configuration Approach
- Environment-based configuration through Supabase client setup
- TypeScript strict mode for type safety
- ESLint configuration for code quality standards

### External Dependencies
- **Next.js 16.3.4**: Modern React framework with App Router
- **Supabase**: Backend-as-a-Service for database, auth, and storage
- **@vladmandic/face-api**: Client-side face recognition library
- **Leaflet**: Interactive mapping functionality
- **Tailwind CSS v4**: Utility-first styling framework

### Integration Points
- **Supabase Storage**: Secure file upload and retrieval for photos
- **Google Fonts**: Optimized font loading with next/font
- **Vercel Analytics**: User behavior tracking and performance monitoring

```mermaid
graph LR
    A[User Interface] --> B[Authentication Service]
    A --> C[Face Recognition Engine]
    A --> D[Map Integration]
    B --> E[Supabase Auth]
    C --> F[Local Face Models]
    D --> G[Leaflet Maps]
    E --> H[PostgreSQL Database]
    F --> I[Vector Similarity Search]
    G --> J[Location Services]
```

## Key Features

### Functionality Overview

**Missing Person Reporting System**
- Comprehensive form for reporting missing individuals with photo upload
- Client-side face analysis to generate embeddings automatically
- Privacy controls for contact information sharing
- Real-time submission feedback and validation

**Public Sighting Submission**
- Intuitive map-based location selection using Leaflet
- Photo upload with automatic face detection
- Optional notes field for additional context
- Anonymous reporting capabilities

**AI-Powered Matching Engine**
- Server-side face similarity comparison using cosine distance
- Multi-tier matching system (strong, notify, possible)
- Confidence scoring with configurable thresholds
- Continuous background matching against new submissions

**Dual-Role Dashboard**
- Separate views for reporters (families) and finders (public)
- Real-time match notifications and status updates
- Contact sharing controls with granular permissions
- Case management workflow from active to resolved

### Implementation Highlights

**Client-Side Face Processing** (`app/report-case/page.tsx`, `app/report-sighting/page.tsx`)
- Browser-based face embedding generation eliminates server load
- Progressive enhancement with fallback handling
- Real-time preview and validation feedback

**Secure API Layer** (`app/api/dashboard/route.ts`)
- Token-based authentication with Supabase JWT verification
- Row-level security enforcement at the API level
- Optimized database queries with proper indexing

**Interactive Mapping** (`components/LocationPickerMap.tsx`)
- Dynamic import to avoid SSR issues with Leaflet
- Geolocation services for precise location capture
- Responsive map interface for mobile devices

### Feature Architecture

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> Idle
    Idle --> ReportCase: Submit Missing Person
    Idle --> ReportSighting: Submit Sighting
    ReportCase --> Processing: Generate Embedding
    ReportSighting --> Processing: Upload & Analyze
    Processing --> Active: Data Stored
    Active --> Matched: AI Detection
    Matched --> ContactShared: Strong Match
    ContactShared --> Resolved: Family Confirms
    Resolved --> [*]: Case Closed
```

The platform represents a sophisticated balance between powerful AI capabilities and user-friendly design, ensuring that technology serves the humanitarian goal of reuniting families while maintaining the highest standards of privacy and security.

</blog>
